hooks.text: The Apollo flag on the Moon never waved.
The flag on the Moon was never moving in wind.
Six American flags were planted on the airless Moon.

title: Why the Apollo 11 Flag Looked Like It Was Waving
description: NASA designed a horizontal rod to hold the Apollo flag extended, but vacuum physics kept the fabric swinging after astronauts planted it.

beats.text: The Apollo flag on the Moon never waved.
beats.visual: Buzz Aldrin saluting the American flag on the Moon during Apollo 11, 1969

beats.text: Earth's atmosphere easily dampens fluttering cloth within seconds.
beats.visual: High speed photo of a fabric flag fluttering in Earth wind

beats.text: But the lunar vacuum has zero air to stop motion.
beats.visual: Apollo 11 Lunar Module on the airless surface of the Moon, 1969

beats.text: NASA added a top horizontal rod to hold the flag fabric open.
beats.visual: Lunar Flag Assembly mechanism on the Apollo Lunar Module ladder, 1969

beats.text: Astronauts physically twisted and jostled the pole while planting it.
beats.visual: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin planting the flag on Apollo 11 TV downlink, 1969

beats.text: Without atmospheric drag, that disturbance made the fabric oscillate like a pendulum.
beats.visual: Apollo 12 Commander Pete Conrad holding the leaning lunar flag, 1969

beats.text: The moment astronauts released the pole, the flag stood completely still.
beats.visual: Apollo 17 Commander Gene Cernan standing beside motionless lunar flag, 1972

beats.text: No real breeze touched any American flag on the Moon.
beats.visual: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter photo of Apollo 12 flag shadow on the Moon, 2012
